sections.heading: Silicone Restoration vs. Full Replacement on Montclair Flat Roofs

c.v: A roof is a coating candidate when the deck and insulation are sound and only the surface has aged.

runs.v: Silicone roof coatings can be applied over existing sound roofing materials without costly tear-offs, and coatings generally suit roofs under about 25 years old, although roof condition matters more than age. A roof with wet insulation, a soft deck, or widespread membrane failure needs a full tear off and a new roof instead, because a coating seals the surface, not the layers under it. About 19% of Montclair's roughly 16,000 housing units sit in two- to four-unit buildings and about 14% in buildings of 20 or more units, per the U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019-2023, and those low-slope roofs are where the choice comes up most.

sections.heading: Our Process for Silicone Roof Coating in Montclair, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing inspects the membrane, seams, flashings, and drainage and confirms the deck and insulation are sound, because recoating fits a roof whose surface has aged over a sound deck.

runs.v: A coating-candidate assessment determines whether to coat as-is, coat after specified repairs, or replace rather than coat, per the RCMA, before work begins on the township's Bloomfield Avenue and Watchung Plaza low-slope roofs.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing cleans and dries the roof, repairs the seams, splits, and flashings, and runs an adhesion test before any field coat.

runs.v: Proper application requires thorough surface preparation: the crew pressure-washes the roof, clears debris, and lets the surface dry fully, because surface cleaning is essential for proper silicone adhesion and a primer is no substitute for it, per the RCMA. Silicone cures with atmospheric moisture yet needs a dry substrate to bond, so the weather is monitored for a proper cure, and an aged asphalt surface takes an epoxy primer to stop bleed-through, per coating manufacturer guidance.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing applies high-solids silicone to the manufacturer dry-film thickness, near 1.5 gallons per 100 square feet for roughly 22 dry mils, because warranty term scales with film thickness.

runs.v: High solids silicone leaves more material after curing, so it builds the film in fewer coats; a renewable manufacturer warranty runs near 10 to 15 years at 20 to 22 mils and 15 to 20 years at 30 mils, per the RCMA and coating manufacturers, and a Newark Quality Roofing lead verifies the dry-film thickness at a final inspection.

How Much Does It Cost to Coat a Roof With Silicone?

Silicone coating typically costs $5.00 to $9.00 per square foot installed, so a 2,000-square-foot storefront roof would typically run about $10,000 to $18,000 before any repairs, and a professionally applied roof coating still costs far less than the replacement cost of a new membrane. Those are typical published figures, not a Newark Quality Roofing quote; the estimate follows the roof size, roof condition, and detail work, and any utility rebates or energy savings vary by building.

sections.heading: What Are the Downsides of Using Silicone Roof Coating?

c.v: Silicone has trade-offs worth weighing before a free estimate.

runs.v: It costs more per square foot than acrylic, and while its water-shedding surface resists mildew, it holds airborne dirt, so reflectance falls as the roof surface ages, and it is slippery when wet. Only silicone sticks to cured silicone, so every future recoat is silicone; it cannot go on a damp surface; and it will not fix wet insulation or a failed deck. ENERGY STAR no longer rates roof coatings, since the EPA ended its ENERGY STAR roof products program in 2022, so compare CRRC cool roof ratings instead.
Which Brand of Silicone Roof Coating Is Considered the Best?

No single brand is best for every roof. Compare silicone systems on ASTM D6694 compliance, solids content, a CRRC cool roof rating, proven performance in ponding water, and the manufacturer warranty terms for the dry-film thickness specified, and ask who applies the coating system and who issues that warranty.

faqs.q: Does silicone roof coating hold up in ponding water on a Montclair flat roof?

runs.v: Yes. A 100% silicone roof coating resists permanent and standing water without softening or losing adhesion, while water-based acrylic re-emulsifies under continuous immersion and most acrylic warranties exclude ponded areas, per the RCMA and coating manufacturers.

faqs.q: Can silicone coating restore a Montclair commercial roof instead of replacing it?

runs.v: Yes, when the deck and insulation stay sound and only the membrane surface has deteriorated; a wet insulation layer or a damaged deck calls for full replacement. Recoating extends service life at a fraction of tear-off cost, and a maintained silicone roof is recoated with silicone at the 15 to 20 year interval rather than torn off, per the RCMA.

faqs.q: Does a silicone coating on a Montclair commercial roof need a permit?

runs.v: A commercial, multi-family, or attached Montclair building crosses into permit territory once roof work exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code, with recover-versus-tear-off limits under N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4. A property in a historic district, or a designated landmark, can need extra review, so confirm with the Montclair construction office before work.

faqs.q: Does silicone roof coating lower energy costs in Montclair?

runs.v: It can lower energy costs on an air-conditioned building: a reflective roof stays more than 50°F cooler than a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon, per the DOE, and a cool roof reduces peak cooling demand by 11 to 27% in air-conditioned residential buildings, per the EPA. The coating adds no meaningful R-value, so the net annual benefit is smaller in Montclair's heating-dominated climate.

faqs.q: How long does silicone roof coating last, and can it be recoated later?

runs.v: A silicone coating carries a renewable 10, 15, or 20 year manufacturer warranty that scales with dry-film thickness, so silicone roof coatings extend service life by roughly 10 to 20 years, and regular maintenance and recoating at the end of the term protect the roof without a tear-off. Cured silicone is recoated with silicone, not acrylic or urethane, per the RCMA and coating manufacturers.
